lab_title: Understanding Retrograde Motion: Earth vs. Heliocentric Perspectives
top_level_objectives: Visualize apparent retrograde motion from the perspective of an Earth-based observer.
Identify the relationship between planetary orbital speeds and the phenomenon of retrograde motion.
Compare the geocentric explanation of epicycles with the heliocentric explanation of relative orbital motion.
Distinguish differences in the retrograde loops of Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn based on their distance from the Sun.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the phenomenon of retrograde motion from a surface-level perspective.
key_visuals: A night sky dome featuring a prominent constellation background with a bright Mars marker.
student_actions: Advance through a simulated timeline of several months to observe Mars changing position relative to the stars.

scenes.brief_purpose: Quantify the observed path of Mars.
key_visuals: A static trace line connecting the points of Mars over time, showing a distinct S-shaped retrograde loop.
student_actions: Trace the path of the loop with their finger to recognize the reversal in direction.

scenes.brief_purpose: Shift the camera to an overhead solar system view.
key_visuals: A top-down view of the inner solar system showing the Sun, Earth, and Mars in their respective orbits.
student_actions: Observe the orbital speeds of Earth and Mars to notice that Earth completes its orbit much faster than Mars.

scenes.brief_purpose: Correlate the relative positions of Earth and Mars to the retrograde loop seen from Earth.
key_visuals: A dual-view split screen comparing the top-down orbital alignment with the Earth-based sky view.
student_actions: Drag a slider to watch the moment Earth passes Mars and observe how the line-of-sight vector creates the apparent backward motion.

scenes.brief_purpose: Test how different outer planets exhibit retrograde motion.
key_visuals: A selection panel to switch the target planet between Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn.
student_actions: Compare the size and duration of the retrograde loops for each planet to note that further planets have smaller, less frequent loops.

scenes.brief_purpose: Reflect on why the heliocentric model succeeds over the geocentric one.
key_visuals: An overlay showing the archaic epicycle model vs the real heliocentric orbital tracks.
student_actions: Toggle between models to confirm that the heliocentric view naturally explains the retrograde loop without requiring complex mathematical epicycles.
